basedOn: Standard physiology: the portal vein delivers absorbed nutrients to the liver for first-pass partitioning - ethanol cleared first, a large fructose load handled hepatically (de novo lipogenesis), otherwise glucose to glycogen and the periphery. Teaching averages.
sources: NIDDK - Your Digestive System & How It Works: https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/digestive-diseases/digestive-system-how-it-works
Hall & Hall, Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed. - Unit XII, Gastrointestinal Physiology
Boron & Boulpaep, Medical Physiology, 3rd ed. - The Gastrointestinal System

inputs.description: Fructose is handled almost entirely first-pass by the liver

firstPass.label: First-pass reception
firstPass.detail: The portal vein delivers absorbed nutrients to the liver, which decides - before anything reaches the rest of the body - what to burn, store, or convert.

hepaticChoice.label: Hepatic priority
hepaticChoice.detail: The liver has a priority order: it clears ethanol first (it's a toxin), routes a fructose load through its own metabolism, and otherwise partitions glucose to glycogen and the periphery.

choices.note: Ethanol is oxidized first - fat oxidation pauses while it clears.
A large fructose load is handled hepatically -> de novo lipogenesis teaching.

alcoholPriority.label: Ethanol first-pass oxidation
alcoholPriority.detail: The liver prioritizes clearing ethanol; fat oxidation is suppressed and dietary fat is more likely stored during the window (energy-partitioning teaching, not a score).

fructoseHandling.label: Fructose hepatic handling
fructoseHandling.detail: Fructose largely bypasses the glucose control step and is metabolized in the liver; a large bolus feeds de novo lipogenesis - the 'fructose tax' narrative.

balancedPartition.label: Balanced partition
balancedPartition.detail: Glucose tops up liver glycogen and passes to the periphery; a normal mixed meal partitions cleanly toward fuel.

handoff.label: Fuel -> systemic circulation
handoff.detail: What survives first-pass enters the general circulation for peripheral delivery.
